items.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Use ONLY the claims in the ESSENCE list below; every paragraph must correspond to at least one essence item (record indices). Do not add doctrines, comparisons, meta-commentary, or quoted terms. ESSENCE: [0] Distinct from every lit thing, light itself does not shine as an object — too pervasive to appear; illumined-vs-illuminator is mere convention.

paragraphs.text: Light itself is different from every lit-up thing: lamps and suns get seen, but light itself never shows up as an object, because it is everywhere already — too spread out to appear. And all our talk of things-that-light-up versus the-lighting itself is just a convenient name we made up.

ESSENCE: [0] Established yet unaccomplishable, non-lord yet lord, place-and-time full of own power — eternal, pervasive: Bhairava-Lord, I praise.

paragraphs.text: Here is a knot that stays tied: consciousness set down from the very start, yet never finishable. The self, no master and yet Master. Its place and time stuffed full with its own power — lasting forever, spread everywhere. Bhairava the Lord: I praise Him.

paragraphs.text: This seven-part good conduct — remember it in your heart once other thoughts have melted away. If you long for the ultimate, you will enter the highest home again and again. And you will come to know the very discussion we are having right now, about the most real thing in all three worlds. Notice what just happened: the song named its own ending.
